Location: shelter yard, the gate seam between kennel run and open pavement
PursuerType: shelter handler with a catch pole, fixed loop along the fence
EscapeCondition: step through the gate seam on the turn after the pole swings, and cross the threshold onto pavement
FailCondition: stand on the gate tile while the pole reaches it; the handler walks you back to the run and the loop restarts unchanged
PlayerSees: The yard gate stands open a dog's width, and a man with a catch pole walks the fence on the same slow loop he has walked all morning. The pole tips left before it comes down, every pass. You wait out his turn, slip the gap, and the pavement keeps going further than the yard ever did.

Location: service alley behind the row shops, dumpsters and stacked crates on both walls
PursuerType: loose yard dog, same lunge pattern on every approach
EscapeCondition: step off the lunge tile while the lunge commits right, then clear two corners
FailCondition: share a tile with the lunge; a shoulder goes into the wall and the chase resets one block back
PlayerSees: Something big comes off the wall behind you and leans right before it lunges, the same lean each time. You step off the tile it is coming to, let it commit to the empty side, and take the corner while it is still turning. Something gave up two corners ago. You keep running anyway.

Location: four-lane arterial, curb to curb, no median
PursuerType: moving traffic, obstacle not pursuer, lanes on a fixed cycle
EscapeCondition: leave the curb on the beat after the horn and cross all four lanes in one unbroken line
FailCondition: stop on a lane tile; horns and brakes push you back to the curb and the lane cycle repeats the same way
PlayerSees: Four lanes, headlights stacked both directions, and nothing out here is chasing you. You read the space between the near truck and the next set of lights, and you take it in one line without stopping in the middle, because the middle is where the road decides for you.

Location: rail yard gravel shoulder alongside a rolling freight
PursuerType: yard patrol dog on the ballast, straight-line runner, no cutting
EscapeCondition: match the car's speed on the shoulder and jump inside the two-turn window the open door gives you
FailCondition: jump short of the door lip; you land on gravel, roll, and the freight takes the opening away
PlayerSees: Gravel, a freight going faster than you are, and one boxcar door already yawning open. Behind you, paws on gravel. You pick the gap and you do not slow down for it, and the floor of the car comes up hard under your chest.

Location: diner back lot, grease bins, chain fence on the far side, alley mouth behind
PursuerType: kitchen hand at the screen door, same two-step out and back
EscapeCondition: leave by the fence side while the door swings, or stay for the paper tray and leave by the fence side after
FailCondition: back out through the alley mouth you came in by; you keep the food and lose the ground, and the yard runs the same two-step next time
PlayerSees: The back door bangs and a hand you don't know puts down a paper tray. You can be gone before it straightens up, or you can eat first and decide about the hand after. Either way the yard has two ways out, and only one of them is forward.

Location: chain link fence line at the lot edge, a scraped hollow under the wire
PursuerType: loose dog off the lot, three-tile sweep it has run on every approach, never varied
EscapeCondition: reach the hollow and go under while the sweep is on its left tile, one clear tile of space between you
FailCondition: take the hollow with the sweep adjacent; the wire and the teeth arrive together and the crossing costs you the rest of the day
PlayerSees: Chain link, a scraped hollow under it, and the thing behind you close enough that you hear it set its feet. It drops the same shoulder it has dropped on every pass. You go under, the wire takes the back leg on the way through, and the back leg has opinions now. You tell it what you told the gate: not yet.
